result.title: Training Dynamics of Transformers on Unbounded Inputs: Attention Learning Can Lag Output Layer Learning
result.summary: The success of transformers is attributed to several factors, including their capacity to express formal languages over variable-length inputs, and ability of the attention mechanism to focus on relevant input features. However, there is limited understanding of the training dynamics of shallow transformers, specifically how to decouple the learning of the attention and the output (feedforward) layer. A natural extension of the theory of one-step gradient feature learning in feedforward networks suggests that one could first learn the attention weights with a single gradient step, and then train the output layer. We show that this fails for a shallow transformer trained to recognize a star-free language from unbounded-length input. We prove that the transformer can be trained to recognize the language with a three-phase gradient descent: the output layer is updated first, followed by an attention update, and the output layer is fine-tuned in the third phase. In contrast, the language cannot be learned by training only the attention or output layer, or by a single attention-layer update followed by finetuning the output layer. We empirically show that ``attention learning lagging output layer learning" is beneficial in other language recognition, regression, and in-context learning tasks as well.

AI.brief_summary: 研究浅层 transformer 在无界长度输入上的训练动力学：证明识别某 star-free 语言无法靠单步注意力更新加微调完成，而需「先更新输出层、再更新注意力、最后微调输出层」的三阶段梯度下降，并在语言识别、回归和 in-context learning 任务上给出经验支持。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「注意力学习滞后于输出层」的分阶段训练结论，可能为 LVR 中注意力/隐状态与答案读出层的训练顺序、轨迹监督与贡献分配提供可核查线索；但该工作是纯文本理论，未涉及视觉证据筛选，迁移需人工判断。
